question: Do you maintain a written information security policy, approved by management and reviewed at least annually?
answer: We maintain a written Information Security Policy (version 3.2), owned by the Head of Platform and approved on 2025-09-15, with an annual review cycle. The 2026 review is overdue. The review and re-approval by our CEO is scheduled for 2026-11-20.

question: Is single sign-on enforced for all workforce access to production systems?
answer: Yes. All workforce access to production goes through Okta SSO; there are no local logins on production systems. Production AWS access is granted through AWS IAM Identity Center federated to Okta, with admin roles assigned to the Engineering group only. GitHub Enterprise and the Ledgerline Admin Console are also Okta-assigned applications.

question: Is multi-factor authentication enforced for ALL workforce accounts (employees and contractors) that can access production systems or customer data?
answer: Yes. MFA (Okta Verify push or WebAuthn) is enforced for every workforce account, employees and contractors, through a single Okta sign-on policy, and there is no password-only rule. question: Describe your password requirements for workforce accounts.
answer: Workforce passwords are governed by the Okta password policy: minimum 14 characters, the last 10 passwords cannot be reused, new passwords are checked against known-breached password lists, and accounts lock after 10 failed sign-in attempts. Passwords do not expire on a fixed schedule.

question: Are user access rights to production reviewed at least quarterly? When was the last review?
answer: Yes. Production access rights are reviewed quarterly in Okta. The most recent review was completed on 2026-10-06; the next is scheduled for January 2027.

question: Is all customer data encrypted at rest? Specify the algorithm and how keys are managed.
answer: Yes. Customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. The production PostgreSQL database (Amazon RDS) and the S3 buckets holding customer statement files and reconciliation exports are encrypted with a customer-managed AWS KMS key that rotates automatically every year. Reconciliation export files created before 2026-11-07 remain encrypted with AES-256 under S3-managed keys until they expire, no later than 2026-12-07.

question: Is customer data encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher?
answer: Yes, for customer traffic over public networks. The public API load balancer serves HTTPS using AWS security policy ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 (TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred). Plain HTTP requests on port 80 are redirected to HTTPS with a 301.

question: Are encryption keys rotated automatically?
answer: Yes. The customer-managed AWS KMS key (alias/ledgerline-data) used for the production database, the customer statements bucket, the audit log bucket and Secrets Manager has automatic key rotation enabled; AWS KMS rotates the key material annually. The production database credential is rotated automatically every 30 days.

question: Are databases holding customer data isolated from the public internet?
answer: Yes. The production PostgreSQL database (Amazon RDS) is not publicly accessible and runs in private subnets. Its security group accepts connections on port 5432 only from the application tier's security group.

question: How are application secrets and credentials stored and rotated?
answer: Application secrets and credentials are stored in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypted with Ledgerline's customer-managed AWS KMS key. The production database credential is rotated automatically every 30 days by a Secrets Manager rotation function. Third-party API keys held in Secrets Manager do not have automatic rotation configured.

question: Are production databases backed up at least daily, with backups retained for at least 30 days?
answer: No. The production database is backed up automatically every night, with point-in-time recovery, but backups are currently retained for 14 days, not 30. Retention was 7 days from March 2026 until 2026-11-07, so the full 14-day history is available from 2026-11-14. Our backup policy requires 35 days, and we plan to restore 35-day retention at our December 2026 review.

question: Are application dependencies scanned automatically for known vulnerabilities at least weekly?
answer: No. Automated dependency vulnerability scanning has not run since June 2026, when our previous scanner was removed from CI. We are enabling GitHub Dependabot by 2026-11-13.

question: When was your most recent independent penetration test, and have all critical and high findings been remediated?
answer: Our most recent independent penetration test was performed by Bramble Security (CREST-accredited) from 2025-04-07 to 2025-04-18, covering the public API, web app, admin console and AWS configuration. It had no Critical findings and two High findings. BR-01 was fixed on 2025-05-02. BR-02 was fixed on 2025-09-03, but Bramble has not yet retested that fix; it will be verified in our next test with Bramble Security, booked for 2026-12-01. No penetration test has been performed since April 2025.

question: Are all code changes peer-reviewed before they reach production?
answer: Yes. Every change to main requires a pull request with an approving review from a code owner, and direct pushes to main are blocked. CI runs tests and lint on every pull request. Production deploys run only from main and require approval from a second engineer through GitHub's protected production environment.

question: Are production, staging and development environments separated?
answer: Yes. Production, staging and development run in separate AWS accounts. Production infrastructure is defined in Terraform with its own state.

question: Do you have a documented incident response plan that is tested at least annually?
answer: Yes. Ledgerline maintains a documented incident response plan with SEV1-SEV3 severity levels and an on-call incident commander. The plan is exercised with a tabletop at least once a year. The most recent was on 2026-02-19 (leaked AWS access key scenario, simulated containment in 38 minutes); both follow-up actions were completed by 2026-03-10.

question: Within what timeframe will you notify Harbor Bank of a security incident affecting our data or services?
answer: We notify Harbor Bank within 36 hours of confirming a security incident affecting Harbor Bank data. If an incident disrupts the services we provide to Harbor Bank for 4 hours or more, we notify Harbor Bank as soon as possible, in line with the bank service provider notification rule.

question: Do you use generative AI or LLM services that process Harbor Bank data? If yes, describe the service, the data sent, and the contractual protections.
answer: Yes. Since our August 2026 release, the reconciliation service uses Anthropic's API (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to draft short exception memos for statement lines that cannot be matched to a ledger entry. For each unmatched line we send the counterparty name, amount, value date and remittance text as they appear on the statement, together with the nearest candidate ledger entries. Under our order form with Anthropic, these inputs are deleted within 30 days and are not used to train models. This use did not go through our vendor security review before launch. The DPA with Anthropic is not yet signed; it is due to be signed by 2026-11-21.

question: How soon after contract termination is Harbor Bank data deleted, including from backups?
answer: Within 30 days of contract termination we delete Harbor Bank data from our production systems. Database backups are currently retained for 14 days and age out after that, so no copy remains in our database backups more than 44 days after termination. If we restore 35-day backup retention, as our backup policy requires, that limit becomes 65 days. Reconciliation exports expire automatically 30 days after they are created. Statement lines sent to Anthropic to draft exception memos are deleted by Anthropic within 30 days under our order form. Our error-monitoring provider (Sentry) keeps data for 30 days and our transactional email provider (Postmark) for 45 days.

answer: Yes. We carry cyber liability insurance with Coalition, with a $5,000,000 aggregate limit. The policy renews on 2027-03-01.

question: Is the production environment deployed across multiple availability zones?

The application tier runs on Amazon ECS on Fargate across the same three availability zones, with a minimum of three tasks.
